title: Decidability of unification in the basic modal logic K
formal: Is there a deterministic Turing machine that halts on every finite modal formula φ and decides whether there exists a substitution σ for its propositional variables such that σ(φ) is valid on every Kripke frame?
context:
Beklemishev's 2025 paper explicitly distinguishes the open K case from solved transitive modal logics.

This short research proposal states the target identified in the September 2026 fundamental-problem search. The references give the source models and related results. The statement has now received a wording review; a comprehensive review of later results and current open status remains outstanding.

definitions: Formulas are finite expressions generated by variables p_i (i∈ℕ), ⊥, negation, conjunction and the unary operator □; other Boolean connectives and ◇ are abbreviations. Variable indices use binary notation and formulas are supplied as fully written syntax trees. A substitution assigns a finite formula to each variable occurring in φ, may use new propositional variables, and extends simultaneously through the connectives and □; it does not substitute recursively inside its newly inserted formulas. There are no distinguished parameters that must remain unchanged. A frame is a nonempty set W with an arbitrary relation R⊆W×W, finite or infinite. A valuation assigns a subset of W to every variable. Satisfaction uses the usual truth tables, ⊥ is false everywhere, and w⊨□ψ iff v⊨ψ for all v with wRv. Validity means satisfaction at every world in every frame with every valuation. This is the basic normal modal logic K, with no reflexivity, transitivity or seriality requirement on R. The substitution is existentially quantified without a length bound. Only its existence is decided; no running-time bound or output unifier is required. Malformed formula encodings are rejected.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or prove its logical negation, using exactly the definitions, hypotheses and quantifier order stated here. The proof must cover the complete target.

sentences: Basic modal logic K interprets formulas on arbitrary accessibility relations between possible worlds.
The problem asks whether it is decidable that a finite formula has a substitution instance valid at every world of every such model.
Substitutions act simultaneously on all input variables, may introduce new variables, and leave no designated parameters fixed.
Frames may be finite or infinite, and no reflexivity or transitivity condition is imposed.
The requested algorithm must halt on every input; its time and the size of a possible substitution have no prescribed bounds.
